evidences.evidence_context: Location attribute calibration of mmWave radar. As mmWave radar is adaptable to various kinds of bad weather, it is first widely used in the field of autonomous driving as a complement to vision and LIDAR [80]. As a result, most of the current location attribute calibration works for mmWave radar are serving for autonomous driving [16, 23, 31, 35, 38–41, 76]. The key task of the calibration is to find the point correspondence: the coordinates of one point under two different coordinate systems, for example, the radar coordinate system and the vehicle/camera/LIDAR coordinate system. They typically leverage the designed calibration target, such as a corner reflector, as the reference point to collect point correspondences in an open environment. However, the traditional method of gathering point correspondences no longer works when the scene changes to indoors due to the rich multipath. Besides, manually measuring the coordinates of the reference points in the indoor physical map coordinate system is impractical when mmWave radars are deployed on a large scale.
